name: Fluoxetine
short: An activating SSRI with 5HT2C antagonism and a very long half-life.
mechanism: Blocks **SERT**; also a **5HT2C antagonist**, which disinhibits NE and DA release and makes it **activating** from the first dose; weak **NET** inhibition only at very high doses. Half-life **2–3 days**; active metabolite about **2 weeks**.

targets.note: Weak; relevant only at very high doses

uses: Unipolar depression (SSRIs are first-line for many depressions)
As a SERT blocker, part of the class used for anxiety disorders, OCD, PTSD, eating disorders and other conditions (Chapter 2 overview)
Only SSRI approved for **bulimia** (higher doses)
With **olanzapine**: treatment-resistant unipolar and bipolar depression
Best matched to reduced positive affect, hypersomnia, psychomotor retardation, apathy, fatigue

facts.text: Entered clinical practice **before molecular clarification of the serotonin transporter site**.
The book’s example of an SSRI at SERT’s **inhibitory allosteric site** (the “front seat” of the transporter wagon), reducing SERT’s affinity for serotonin.
Combined with **olanzapine** for bipolar depression and treatment-resistant unipolar depression; 5HT2C antagonism of both may contribute.
Long half-life reduces **withdrawal** reactions but means slow washout before starting drugs such as an **MAOI**; available once daily and **once weekly**.

sideEffects.e: Unwanted activation, even panic, in agitated, anxious or insomniac patients

name: Sertraline
short: SSRI with weak DAT inhibition and σ1 binding.
mechanism: Blocks **SERT**; also weakly inhibits **DAT** (clinical relevance debated, though a little DAT inhibition may aid energy, motivation and concentration) and binds **σ1** receptors.
uses: Unipolar major depression
Anxiety disorders, PTSD, OCD, premenstrual dysphoric disorder, eating disorders (class uses)
Mild activation may help **atypical depression** (hypersomnia, low energy, mood reactivity)
Possible advantage in **psychotic/delusional depression** (σ1)
With bupropion (“Well-oft”)

sideEffects.e: Early side effects that fade with time
sideEffects.via: Acute 5HT at unwanted receptors; tolerance as postsynaptic receptors desensitize

facts.text: σ1 actions may contribute to anxiolytic effects and benefit in psychotic and delusional depression.
Combined with **brexpiprazole** for PTSD in testing at publication.

name: Paroxetine
short: Calming SSRI with mild anticholinergic, weak NET and NOS-inhibiting actions.
mechanism: Blocks **SERT**; mild **M1** antagonism (calming, even sedating early), weak **NET** inhibition (may add antidepressant action at high doses) and inhibition of **nitric oxide synthase**.
uses: Unipolar major depression
Anxiety disorders, PTSD, OCD, premenstrual dysphoric disorder, eating disorders (class uses)

sideEffects.e: Early side effects that fade with time
sideEffects.via: Acute 5HT at unwanted receptors; tolerance as postsynaptic receptors desensitize

sideEffects.e: Notorious **withdrawal**: akathisia, restlessness, GI upset, dizziness, tingling

facts.text: A **controlled-release** form may reduce side effects including discontinuation reactions.

name: Fluvoxamine
short: SSRI with potent σ1 binding; an OCD drug in the US.
mechanism: Blocks **SERT** and binds **σ1** sites more potently than sertraline; preclinical data suggest it may be a σ1 **agonist**, possibly adding anxiolytic action.
uses: **OCD** (never approved for depression in the US)
Depression elsewhere; one of the first SSRIs launched worldwide
Psychotic/delusional depression
CR form: high remission in **OCD** and **social anxiety disorder**

sideEffects.e: Early side effects that fade with time
sideEffects.via: Acute 5HT at unwanted receptors; tolerance as postsynaptic receptors desensitize

facts.text: The **controlled-release** form allows once-daily dosing (IR often twice daily) and may cause less peak-dose sedation.

name: Citalopram
short: Racemic SSRI; the R enantiomer adds antihistamine action and may hinder SERT inhibition.
mechanism: A racemic mixture of **R and S** enantiomers. S inhibits **SERT**; R carries weak **antihistamine** action and may act at SERT in a way that **interferes** with S, reducing net SERT inhibition, especially at low doses.
uses: Unipolar depression; favorable findings in the **elderly**

sideEffects.e: Early side effects that fade with time
sideEffects.via: Acute 5HT at unwanted receptors; tolerance as postsynaptic receptors desensitize

sideEffects.e: **QTc prolongation** at higher doses (limits dose increases)

facts.text: Generally well tolerated but somewhat **inconsistent** at the lowest dose, often needing a dose increase that QTc concerns limit.
Limited efficacy for depression in dementia; may help **agitation**, but prolongs **QT**.

name: Escitalopram
short: The pure S enantiomer of citalopram: the “quintessential SSRI.”
mechanism: The active **S enantiomer** of citalopram, without the R enantiomer. **Pure SERT inhibition** explains almost all of its actions.
uses: Unipolar major depression
Anxiety disorders, PTSD, OCD, premenstrual dysphoric disorder, eating disorders (class uses)

sideEffects.e: Early side effects that fade with time
sideEffects.via: Acute 5HT at unwanted receptors; tolerance as postsynaptic receptors desensitize

facts.text: No antihistamine action, no higher-dose **QTc** restriction, lowest dose predictably effective; perhaps the **best-tolerated** SSRI with the **fewest CYP450 interactions**.
May match citalopram in dementia without **QT** prolongation; SSRIs/SNRIs may help apathy in FTD.

name: Vilazodone
nbn: Serotonin reuptake inhibitor and 5HT1A partial agonist
short: SPARI: SERT inhibition plus 5HT1A partial agonism in one molecule.
mechanism: Inhibits **SERT** and is a **5HT1A partial agonist**. About half of SERTs and half of 5HT1A receptors are occupied immediately; partial agonism at somatodendritic autoreceptors speeds their **desensitization**, and postsynaptic 5HT1A action may release **dopamine** downstream.
uses: Unipolar depression

sideEffects.e: Less sexual dysfunction and weight gain (observed)
sideEffects.via: Downstream DA release from 5HT1A partial agonism

facts.text: Recreates in one drug the long-used strategy of adding a 5HT1A partial agonist (buspirone, aripiprazole, brexpiprazole, cariprazine, quetiapine) to an SSRI, avoiding drug interactions and off-target effects.
Should theoretically be **anxiolytic** (SERT inhibition + 5HT1A partial agonism); an off-label option for anxiety.

name: Vortioxetine
short: SERT inhibitor with 5HT3/5HT7 antagonism, 5HT1A agonism and 5HT1B/D partial agonism; pro-cognitive.
mechanism: Inhibits **SERT**; **5HT3** antagonist (one of its most potent actions) and **5HT7** antagonist; **5HT1A agonist**; weak **5HT1B/D** partial agonist/antagonist. Some actions raise 5HT further (SERT, 5HT1B/D, 5HT7), others release **DA, NE, ACh and histamine** (5HT1A, 5HT1B heteroreceptors, 5HT3).

targets.note: One of its most potent actions

uses: Antidepressant; possibly pro-cognitive (Table 3-2)
Unipolar depression with **cognitive symptoms**: superior on the **DSST** (processing speed)

facts.text: A **5HT3 antagonist** with pro-cognitive and antidepressant actions (Table 3-2).
The DSST samples attention, executive function, memory and mostly **processing speed** (the “Fab Four”); vortioxetine improves it more than other antidepressants.

nbn: Serotonin reuptake inhibitor and receptor modulator (multimodal)
